import pandas as pd

# File paths for the sources
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_76/test_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_76/test_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_76/test_2.csv"

# Load Source 0
# Schema: ['Rank', 'Code', 'Description', 'x(t)']
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path)

# Load Source 1
# Schema: ['Code', 'Description']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path)

# Load Source 2
# Schema: ['FL_DATE', 'UNIQUE_CARRIER', 'FL_NUM', 'ORIGIN_AIRPORT_ID', 'ORIGIN_CITY_MARKET_ID', 'DEST_AIRPORT_ID', 'DEST_CITY_MARKET_ID']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path)

# Transformation plan:
# Target schema: ['Code': int, 'Rank': int, 'Description_x': str, 'Description_y': str]
#
# Observations:
# - Source0 has Rank, Code, Description (which can be Description_x)
# - Source1 has Code, Description (can be Description_y)
# - Source2 has flight info, including FL_NUM which matches Rank in Source0, and DEST_AIRPORT_ID which can be linked to Code in Source0 or Source1
#
# Since the target examples show Description_x and Description_y are very similar or identical descriptions of airports,
# and Code and Rank come from Source0,
# the best approach is to join Source0 and Source1 on Code to get Description_x (from Source0.Description) and Description_y (from Source1.Description).
#
# Source2 does not have Description columns, only airport IDs and flight info, so it is not directly useful for Description columns.
# Also, Source2.FL_NUM matches Source0.Rank, but no Description in Source2.
#
# Therefore, the main join is:
#   df0 (Rank, Code, Description) LEFT JOIN df1 (Code, Description) ON Code
# Rename df0.Description -> Description_x
# Rename df1.Description -> Description_y
#
# Output columns: Code (int), Rank (int), Description_x (str), Description_y (str)
#
# Finally, write the result to the target CSV.

# Rename Description columns before join to avoid collision
df0_renamed = df0.rename(columns={"Description": "Description_x"})
df1_renamed = df1.rename(columns={"Description": "Description_y"})

# Merge on 'Code'
df_merged = pd.merge(df0_renamed, df1_renamed[['Code', 'Description_y']], on='Code', how='left')

# Select and reorder columns as per target schema
target_df = df_merged[['Code', 'Rank', 'Description_x', 'Description_y']]

# Ensure correct dtypes
target_df['Code'] = target_df['Code'].astype(int)
target_df['Rank'] = target_df['Rank'].astype(int)
target_df['Description_x'] = target_df['Description_x'].astype(str)
target_df['Description_y'] = target_df['Description_y'].astype(str)

# Write to target CSV
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_76/target_multisource_cot.csv"
target_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
